text.p: Pakistan's ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto, thronged by chanting supporters, moved out of her official residence into a private home on Tuesday, one week after being sacked on disputed charges of corruption.

"I think this whole thing stinks," an embittered Bhutto told an impromptu news conference at the home of Senator Gulzar Ahmed, where she will temporarily stay with her three children after vacating the prime minister's stately mansion.

About 200 activists from her Pakistan People's Party mobbed the black BMW sedan carrying Bhutto after it passed through the iron gates outside the prime minister's residence on its way to Ahmed's house in the capital Islamabad.

A crowd quickly surrounded the car, forcing it to stop. "Go Leghari, go!" the activists shouted, denouncing President Farooq Leghari, who dissolved the National Assembly and dismissed Bhutto's three-year-old government last week.
"Benazir step forward, we are with you!" the party workers chanted as they escorted the car the short distance to Ahmed's house, where dozens of supporters forced their way in.

Bhutto, holding her three-year-old daughter Asifa on her lap, told reporters that her lawyers expected to file a legal petition on Wednesday morning asking the Supreme Court to reinstate her. "I look forward for early relief by the Supreme Court. I repudiate the charges the president has made," she said.
